implementation_schedule.summary: How the implementation roles of one Delivery Item write: one after another in their approved order, or at the same time in lanes whose approved write scopes are disjoint.

values.tradeoffs: Implementation roles write one after another in their approved order in the Item worktree. Today's behaviour and the baseline lanes are measured against; the slowest path when the plan gives each role its own files.

Implementation roles whose approved lane scopes are disjoint write at the same time in the one Item worktree, ordered only by declared seams, and the coordinator stays the only committer. Shorter implementation wall time, while the plan must declare lane scopes and seams, seam defects surface only at the frozen candidate and token cost per Item rises.

implementation_schedule.metric: Per Item with 2 or more implementation roles besides the Software Architect: implementation wall time from the first implementation role's start to the candidate freeze against the sum of its lane times, mean concurrent writer lanes, lane scope violations found before the coordinator's commit, seam-related critical or major code review findings, QA failures at a seam and environment collisions.

promotion.unit: At least 3 Items with 2 or more implementation roles besides the Software Architect run with parallel_lanes_v1, from at least 2 Deliveries.
promotion.threshold: Implementation wall time at most 70% of the lane-time sum, zero lane scope violations, seam-related critical or major findings per Item no higher than the sequential baseline and zero environment collisions, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

review_panels.summary: How backlog epic and root, Solution Design, Design System and Operation contract reviews read the reviewed document.

values.tradeoffs: One fresh reviewer per review step reads every lens on its role's own tier. Today's behaviour and the baseline the panel is measured against; the slowest path, since one reader works through every lens in turn.

One fresh read-only reader per lens assignment runs in parallel and replaces the step's reviewer; the read-only reviewer roles run as their lens-tier variants. Shorter review wall time, while valid-major recall is still measured against the single reader and a panel major can be overrated.

lens_panel.description: Lens-tier reader variant for review panels.

review_panels.metric: Per review pass on the same document, the panel's valid critical and major findings against the official single-reader review's, and the panel's wall time against the official review's.

promotion.unit: At least 5 panel review passes across at least 2 flows.
promotion.threshold: Panel valid-major recall at least equal to the official review's and panel wall time at most 50% of it, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

mechanical_pass_tier.summary: Which tier runs a backlog, Operation contract or Solution Design writer pass that only applies the fixes a review verdict names, and whether a compiler render, stamp or check step spawns a role at all.

values.tradeoffs: Every writer pass runs on its role's own tier, usually as the resumed writer that still holds the document, and compiler steps run as each flow describes. Today's behaviour and the baseline the mechanical tier is measured against; a pass that only applies spelled-out fixes still generates every edit at the writer's full tier.

A writer pass whose findings each name their exact fix runs on the owning writer's -mechanical variant, a fresh agent on the lower mechanical tier, and render, stamp and check steps run as direct entry commands with no role pass. Shorter fix passes, while the fresh variant re-reads what a resumed writer held and a lower tier may misapply a fix, which the unchanged re-check catches at the cost of a round.

mechanical.description: Lower-tier variant for mechanical passes that apply only the fixes a review verdict names.

mechanical_pass_tier.metric: Per mechanical pass, its wall time and output tokens against the base writer's median for the same pass kind, whether the re-check finds the fix incomplete or wrong (rework), and any unrelated edit the re-check finds.

promotion.unit: A frozen-task A/B that sets the mechanical tier's host values, then at least 3 Deliveries run with mechanical.
promotion.threshold: Median apply_findings wall time at most 50% of the base writer's median for the same pass kind, a rework rate no higher than role_tier's over the same period and zero accepted unrelated edits, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.

review_loop.summary: How a review loop treats the findings a review returns: which findings start a round, where a minor finding goes, what a re-review reads and whether an independent reader calibrates a critical or major claim before it gates, for backlog, Solution Design, Design System and Operation contract reviews and Delivery code review.

values.tradeoffs: Every review loop runs as today, the baseline the other value is measured against. Operation and Design System reviews have no minor rule or re-review scope, so a review that approves with only minor findings can still take a fix pass and a recheck, a code review minor stays a note with no owner, and every critical or major claim gates as returned.

Only a critical or major finding starts a round, and only once one fresh calibration reader confirms it. A minor finding becomes a follow-up with an owner role and a revisit trigger, and a re-review reads only the open blocking findings, the changed text and its dependency context. Shorter review loops, while calibration adds a few minutes whenever a major is real, a wrong downgrade can hide a defect until the shadow judge audits it, and a changed-text re-review can miss a knock-on effect outside the dependency context it is given.

review_loop.metric: Per reviewed document against its matching baseline: review-loop minutes from review start to final verdict, fixes included; rounds; minor findings fixed in a blocking pass against those recorded as follow-ups; and calibration counts, claimed, confirmed, downgraded and invalid, with calibration minutes.

promotion.unit: At least 5 reviewed documents across at least 2 flows: a contract revision, an epic or root review, a Solution or Design System review, or an Item code review.
promotion.threshold: Median review-loop minutes at most 50% of the matching baseline, zero valid critical or major findings found later in the same document and traced to a skipped minor round or a calibration downgrade, the shadow judge confirming every downgrade, and an owner role and revisit trigger on every follow-up, with every shared quality guard holding and the owner's approval.
